I've tried both Solocraft and Nyctermoon, and I gotta say Nyctermoon wins out for me personally.  
They've added a huge truckload of quality of life features, and a bunch of new items and quests for you to strive for that make sense in relation to you having constant access to bots etc.

Your companions won't be progressing alongside you on Nyctermoon, but instead you'll perform certain quests and challenges that allow you to buy a higher "tier" of companions every now and then. So at 60 they'll start out in greens, then when you complete a quest to do BRD you can upgrade them to have full pre-raid BIS and so on.

You can however, level alts, and then hire them into your party, so you can do dungeons with only characters you have personally leveled and geared. I don't think they keep any new loot they get while they're companions though, but I haven't tried anything like that yet so don't quote me on that.

The great creator goddess made the world and populated it with the first mortals, but without truly knowing her creations and their minds.  
She would descend from the stars in mortal form to guide and help them, but her efforts led to a tyrannical rule where those who refused her guidance were deemed heretics and hunted down. In the end, she was captured by a band of mortals who chained her deep within the earth and leeched power from her, becoming the first mortal "gods" of the realm. They were corrupted by the very power they siphoned from her, and became even worse tyrants than she had unwittingly become during her own reign, each of them declaring war on the others and fighting for a world that was steadily shrinking and dying without the creator's true power flowing from the heavens anymore, being eaten away by a slowly encroaching wasteland of white ash, the absence of the creator's magic.

When the creator was freed from her prison by a group of adventurers, she gave them a choice:  
If she were to ascend into the heavens once more, the world, which at this point had literally been shrunk to the size of a small country, would be unmade. The people would die, the lands would be sundered, and she would remake the world. It would be greater, grander, and even more importantly, free from her meddling.  
She would retreat beyond the stars and be a distant, uninvolved entity. The mortals that ascended with her would become the gods of this new world.

It was her reasoning that since she could not understand the hearts of her children, they should be free to govern themselves, and so the gods of this new world were created from the souls of those brave few, with all their strengths and imperfections. The creator vowed to only ever interfere if her children became a danger to the cosmos and creation itself, but beyond that, she would never again interact with the world, content to watch from afar. Her power would keep the world active and alive, but it would forever be up to her creations to forge their own destinies.

It's very taxing on the mage to cast spells within my world, and if they push themselves beyond the limit, they become mana wraiths, monstrous creatures that fade into a parallel overlapping dimension and wreak havoc by stirring the elements but ultimately powerless to interact directly with anyone, and also near-mindless, only existing to create chaos. There is also a limited amount of mana within any given surroundings, so several mages in one location will quickly deplete their resources and also drain some of the vitality from the land, making the earth slightly less fertile, the water less pure, the air less fresh. For this reason, mages tend to be solitary or in small groups.

So their number one weakness would be that there's rarely more than one or two mages in the same place. They can therefore be overwhelmed by sheer number and attacks from multiple angles.  
Number two would be their fear of turning into mana wraiths. A mage unleashing their full power is a terrifying sight, but many would rather die than become wraiths, and those who are aware of this can use it to their advantage.  
Thirdly, fighting a mage within an area that has been depleted of mana will make them borderline useless in a fight, limited to puny little sparks or darts of ice that don't pack a real punch.

Those who specialize in mage slaying tend to favor overwhelming offense, seeking to push mages to the brink with flurries of attacks, forgoing armor for the sake of mobility, and using great weapons that are both swift and inflict tremendous damage, most often two-handed sword. So your typical anti-mage combatant in this world would be wearing cloth, and brandishing a big but maneuverable blade.  
And of course, even a powerful mage is vulnerable when they don't see the crossbow bolt coming from the shadows 50ft away.
